children: New Delhi, Sept. 8 -- Stocks To Trade Ex-Dividend Today: Shares of Force Motors, JBM Auto, Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilisers and Chemicals, are attracting heightened investors' interest on Tuesday, September 8, as it will be the last day to qualify for their scheduled dividend payout.

Nearly twenty companies, including JBM Auto, Force Motors, GNFC, Aastha Spintex, National Fittings, Empire Industries, and Jyoti Resins, have fixed Wednesday, September 9, as the record date for dividend payout. As India follows the T+1 settlement cycle, September 8 is effectively the last trading day to buy and qualify for the corporate action. This means investors must own these stocks during Tuesday's trading to become eligible for the dividend payout.

Force Motors' board of directors announced a final dividend of Rs.50 per equity share with a face value of Rs.10. The company has set Wednesday, September 9, as the record date to determine investors' eligibility for the payout. Hence, investors must own the stock before the record date, making Tuesday the last day to buy the auto stock for the payout. Force Motors' share price was trading marginally lower at Rs.17660 per share on BSE during Tuesday's intraday trading session.

Gujarat Narmada Valley's board of directors announced 210% dividend for the financial year 2025-26. The fertiliser Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) stock will trade ex-dividend on Wednesday, September 9. The board had announced a final dividend of Rs.21 per share. The PSU stock was trading 1.48% lower at Rs.588.75 per share on BSE at 10:12 am on Tuesday.

JBM Auto's board of directors approved an 85% final dividend for the financial year 2025-26. The auto components maker had announced Rs.0.85 dividend per share with a face value of Re 1 each. It had fixed September 9 as the dividend record date. The auto ancillary stock was trading 0.49% higher at Rs.616.9 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.14,589.33 crore at 10:22 am on Tuesday.

The Indian stock market started on a muted note on Tuesday with the Nifty 50 opening below 23,700. BSE Sensex was down close to 0.4%. Banking and financial services stock remained under pressure with ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Union Bank, and HDFC Bank emerging as the top laggards. Broad market indices opened in red with Nifty 100, Nifty 200, Nifty 500, etc., down close to 0.18%. BEL, HINDALCO, HDFC Life, Hindustan Unilever, and Nestle India were among the top Nifty 50 gainers during Tuesday's trading session.
